epics.title: Epidemiological Material Management
epics.jtbd: When an editor has new or updated epidemiological data, I want to draft, review, and publish it into the knowledge base, so that the collection remains accurate and available to readers.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease average time to publish a new material from submission to availability
requirements: R1: An editor can draft and submit a new epidemiological material or protocol.
R2: An editor can edit and update existing materials.
R3: An editor can approve and publish a material for general availability.
R4: An editor can see when a material has become stale and update or unpublish it.
R5: An administrator can view the complete inventory of the collection.
R6: An administrator can see usage metrics (what is actually used) and freshness (what has gone stale).
R7: Any destructive action (like unpublishing or deleting) must be reversible or confirmed before it happens.
R8: What the user types during material drafting must survive a failed submit or lost connection.

slices.title: Material Management Database Schema
slices.jtbd: When implementing data persistence for this epic, I want to define the schema for materials, versions, and statuses, so that the system can reliably store the knowledge base inventory.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new material draft, When it is saved to the database, Then a new record with 'draft' status and version information is persisted
Given a schema migration, When applied, Then the materials table is created with proper constraints
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero schema integrity violations during testing

slices.title: Material Management API Contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing the shared API for this epic, I want to define the endpoints for CRUD operations on materials, so that backend and frontend can build in parallel.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API contract, When a frontend developer reads it, Then they know the exact request and response shapes for creating and fetching materials
Given a contract definition, When automated tools parse it, Then it validates as a correct OpenAPI specification
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero integration failures due to mismatched data shapes

slices.title: Material Management Backend Services
slices.jtbd: When implementing the backend for this epic, I want to build the API endpoints for managing materials, so that the frontend can execute editor commands.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid draft payload, When the POST /materials endpoint is called, Then the material is saved and returned
Given a delete command, When executed, Then the material is soft-deleted to allow reversal
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Endpoint response time under 200ms

slices.title: Material Management Frontend Editor
slices.jtbd: When implementing the UI for this epic, I want to build the editor interface for managing epidemiological materials, so that users can interact with the knowledge base intuitively.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an editor on a mobile phone, When they open the material creation form, Then the form is fully usable and responsive
Given an editor filling a form, When the connection drops and they submit, Then the typed content is preserved locally
Given the UI, When tested for accessibility, Then it meets WCAG 2.1 AA standards including keyboard operability and 4.5:1 text contrast
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero WCAG AA compliance violations in the editor flows

slices.title: Material Management QA & E2E Validation
slices.jtbd: When verifying this epic, I want to test the full lifecycle of a material from drafting to publishing, so that the system correctly supports the editorial workflow.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a test environment, When the automated E2E suite runs, Then it successfully drafts, edits, publishes, and unpublishes a material
Given the API integration tests, When executed, Then all endpoints respond correctly according to the OpenAPI contract
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% test coverage of the critical material management paths

epics.title: Knowledge Base Search and Discovery
epics.jtbd: When a reader is looking for epidemiological information, I want to search and view published materials, so that I can quickly find the protocols I need.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Increase search success rate (queries leading to a viewed material)
requirements: R1: A user can search for epidemiological materials by keywords or tags.
R2: A user can view the full content of a published protocol or material.
R3: The system provides clear visible feedback if a search returns no results.
R4: The system tracks views on materials to feed usage metrics.
R5: The discovery interface is usable on a mobile phone.

slices.title: Search API Contract
slices.jtbd: When defining the search API for this epic, I want to specify the search and view endpoints, so that backend and frontend can implement discovery features in parallel.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the API contract, When viewed by a developer, Then search query parameters and response formats are fully documented
Given an automated contract checker, When run, Then the search API definition passes validation
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero integration bugs for the search endpoint

slices.title: Search and Retrieval Backend
slices.jtbd: When implementing the search functionality for this epic, I want to build the backend logic for finding and serving published materials, so that readers can query the knowledge base.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a search query for 'virus', When the GET /search endpoint is called, Then a paginated list of matching published materials is returned
Given a request to view a material, When the GET /materials/{id} is called, Then the content is returned and a view event is recorded
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Search endpoint response time under 300ms

slices.title: Search and Discovery Frontend
slices.jtbd: When implementing the discovery UI for this epic, I want to build the search interface and material viewer, so that readers can comfortably find and read protocols on any device.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a user on a mobile device, When they search and view a document, Then the layout adapts to the screen size flawlessly
Given a search that yields no results, When the results load, Then visible feedback indicating 'no results found' is explicitly shown
Given the UI, When tested for accessibility, Then it meets WCAG 2.1 AA standards (keyboard navigation, 4.5:1 contrast)
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero layout breaks on standard mobile viewports

slices.title: Search and Discovery QA
slices.jtbd: When verifying this epic, I want to test the end-to-end search and view flows, so that we ensure readers can reliably discover content.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the automated E2E suite, When it executes the discovery path, Then it successfully searches for a term, clicks a result, and views the material
Given a search for a non-existent term, When executed, Then the test asserts that the 'no results' feedback is displayed
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% test pass rate for search critical paths

epics.title: System Outcome Measurement
epics.jtbd: When operating the knowledge base, I want to measure whether it actually reduces the time required to find relevant protocols and keeps content fresh, so that we know if the product is succeeding.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Implement tracking for the GQM primary metrics
requirements: R1: Goal: The knowledge base successfully delivers relevant epidemiological protocols and keeps them fresh.
R2: Question 1: Are users successfully finding materials, or abandoning searches?
R3: Metric 1: Search success rate (percentage of searches that lead to a material view vs. zero-result/abandoned).
R4: Question 2: Is the knowledge base content remaining fresh and useful?
R5: Metric 2: Content freshness (Percentage of viewed materials that were updated in the last year).
R6: The system exposes these specific Goal-Question-Metric measurements on an internal dashboard.

slices.title: GQM Analytics API Contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing the shared API for this epic, I want to define the endpoints for GQM metrics, so that backend and frontend can build in parallel.
slices.acceptanceCriteria: Given the API contract, When a frontend developer reads it, Then they know the exact request and response shapes for the metrics dashboard.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero integration failures due to mismatched metric shapes

slices.title: GQM Analytics Backend
slices.jtbd: When implementing analytics for this epic, I want to build the backend telemetry tracking and aggregation, so that the specific GQM metrics are calculated.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a user performing searches and views, When these events occur, Then they are recorded in the analytics store with relevant timestamps
Given a request for the dashboard metrics, When the endpoint is called, Then the search success rate and content freshness metrics are correctly calculated and returned
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% accuracy in event recording for GQM metrics

slices.title: GQM Dashboard UI
slices.jtbd: When implementing the dashboard for this epic, I want to display the specific GQM metrics, so that stakeholders can see the product's actual performance.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an administrator, When they visit the analytics dashboard, Then they see the stated Goal, Questions, and the calculated Metrics clearly displayed
Given the UI, When tested for accessibility, Then it meets WCAG 2.1 AA standards
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero errors in displaying the calculated metrics on the dashboard

slices.title: GQM QA Validation
slices.jtbd: When verifying the measurement epic, I want to ensure the metrics accurately reflect user behavior, so that we can trust the product analytics.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a simulated user session with a successful search, When the metrics are recalculated, Then the search success rate increases accordingly
Given a simulated session with an abandoned search, When the metrics are recalculated, Then the search success rate decreases accordingly
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero discrepancy between simulated events and reported dashboard metrics

epics.title: Factory Acceptance Content
epics.jtbd: When accepting the delivered system, I want to see a deployed instance with real epidemiological content, so that I can verify all functional paths are walkable in a production-like state.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Complete 100% of the mandatory acceptance paths on the deployed instance
requirements: R1: The deployed instance is reachable by the client from outside the factory.
R2: The instance holds a realistic initial body of epidemiological materials and protocols in Russian, sufficient to exercise cataloging and searching.
R3: One complete traversal of creating, publishing, searching, and viewing a material has been performed on the instance.
R4: The instance is recognisably the client's own, using their language and realistic domain data.

slices.title: Initial Content Seeding Script
slices.jtbd: When preparing the initial instance for this epic, I want to create a database seeder with realistic Russian epidemiological materials, so that the knowledge base is not empty upon delivery.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an empty database, When the seed script is run, Then a realistic set of epidemiological protocols (in Russian) is inserted into the materials table
Given the seeded instance, When an administrator views the inventory, Then they see recognizable, domain-specific content
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of seed data successfully loaded without constraint errors

slices.title: Acceptance Traversal QA
slices.jtbd: When verifying the deployed instance for this epic, I want to execute a complete manual and automated traversal of all paths, so that we prove the system is fully operational.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the deployed instance reachable from outside, When the QA performs a complete traversal (create, publish, search, view), Then the entire flow succeeds without errors
Given the instance UI, When reviewed, Then it correctly displays the Russian language and realistic content
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero blocking defects during the final acceptance traversal

epics.title: Business Continuity and Backups
epics.jtbd: When operating the knowledge base, I want to ensure the system and its epidemiological data are backed up and restorable, so that critical business information is never permanently lost.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Reduce mean time to recovery (MTTR) via verified backups
requirements: R1: The system performs regular automated backups of the epidemiological database.
R2: A complete restore from a backup has been actually performed and verified on a test instance.

slices.title: Automated Backup Configuration
slices.jtbd: When implementing continuity for this epic, I want to configure automated database backups, so that disaster recovery is possible.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the production database, When the backup schedule triggers, Then a secure, encrypted backup archive is generated and stored off-site
Given a backup archive, When inspected, Then it contains a complete snapshot of the database
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% backup completion rate over a 7-day period

slices.title: Backup Restore Verification QA
slices.jtbd: When verifying business continuity for this epic, I want to perform an actual restore from a backup, so that we prove the backups are valid and usable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an automated backup archive, When the restore procedure is executed on a clean test instance, Then the database is completely recovered without data corruption
Given the restored instance, When queried, Then all expected epidemiological materials are present and accessible
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero data loss detected during the restore verification test

epics.title: Identity and Access Management
epics.jtbd: When accessing the system, I want to authenticate securely and recover my account if needed, so that only authorized editors can change the knowledge base.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Decrease time to recover a locked-out account via self-service
requirements: R1: Editors and administrators can securely log into the system.
R2: A self-service recovery path exists for a locked-out account, including the owner account.
R3: The system distinguishes between authenticated editor/admin access and public read access (if applicable).

slices.title: IAM API Contract
slices.jtbd: When implementing the shared API for this epic, I want to define the endpoints for authentication and recovery, so that backend and frontend can build in parallel.
slices.acceptanceCriteria: Given the API contract, When a frontend developer reads it, Then they know the exact request and response shapes for login and account recovery.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero integration failures due to mismatched IAM shapes

slices.title: IAM Backend and Security
slices.jtbd: When implementing authentication for this epic, I want to build secure login and account recovery flows, so that user identities are protected.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given valid credentials, When a user logs in, Then they are authenticated and receive a secure session token
Given a locked-out user, When they request a password reset, Then a secure, time-limited recovery link is sent to their registered email
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero security vulnerabilities in the authentication and recovery flows

slices.title: IAM Frontend Interfaces
slices.jtbd: When building the UI for this epic, I want to create the login and account recovery screens, so that users can access their accounts.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an unauthenticated user, When they attempt to access an editor route, Then they are redirected to the login screen
Given a user on the login screen, When they click 'forgot password', Then they are taken to the self-service recovery form
Given the IAM UI, When tested for accessibility, Then it meets WCAG 2.1 AA standards
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero authentication flow blockers on mobile devices

slices.title: IAM E2E Validation QA
slices.jtbd: When verifying the IAM epic, I want to test the complete login and recovery workflows, so that no user is permanently locked out.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a test user account, When the automated test attempts login with valid credentials, Then access is granted
Given a test user initiating account recovery, When the recovery link is used, Then the password is successfully reset and access is restored
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% success rate for automated login and recovery E2E tests
